A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same avatar-deblurring work despite a changed title and substantial reorganization. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on synthetic ZJU-MoCap data and a captured multi-camera dataset, including baseline comparisons and ablations in Tables 2–9.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds robustness tests, AMASS-driven animation results, and an iPhone capture demonstration.

M1.justification: The reported inter-frame regularizer changes from L2 distance in v1 Equation 15 to geodesic distance in v2 Equation 9. The B-spline motion model, pose displacements, LBS refinement, Gaussian rendering, and image-averaging pipeline otherwise remain.

E1.justification: The synthetic and captured multi-camera benchmarks remain. v2 adds out-of-domain AMASS motions for novel-pose animation and monocular iPhone 16 Pro footage (Figures 13–14), substantially extending evaluation beyond the original multi-view reconstruction scenarios.

E2.justification: GauHuman and the ShiftNet, RVRT, VRT, and BSST plus GauHuman baselines remain unchanged. v2 Table 5 adds Slerp as an explicitly evaluated trajectory alternative to the proposed B-spline representation, expanding comparison methods within the interpolation analysis.

E3.justification: Synthetic blur preprocessing changes from eight RIFE intermediate frames to 16. New evaluation designs vary training views between two, three, and four, perturb SMPL initialization using uniform noise, and compare alternative mask constructions. These are substantial protocol additions; the PDFs do not establish that retained benchmark scores were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds trajectory-representation comparisons, initialization perturbations, freezing all SMPL parameters, mask-quality controls, and view-count ablations. It also extends control-knot and virtual-frame sensitivity analyses to real data. Existing component, regularization, and blur-magnitude ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. v2's random initialization perturbations constitute robustness testing rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and existing component-ablation numbers remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial quantitative robustness results and qualitative animation and smartphone results. Its high-blur comparison also revises the Ours entries: at Kblur=7, PSNR changes from 25.113 to 25.155, now matching the existing full-model ablation result. This is not evidence of a newly established same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The regularizer's mathematical distance changes from L2 to geodesic distance. The continuous blur equation also drops v1's normalization factor, although normalized discrete averaging remains. The B-spline formulation is retained, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first direct reconstruction of sharp, animatable Gaussian avatars from blurry videos through joint motion/avatar optimization, introduce synthetic and captured benchmarks, and claim superiority over the evaluated baselines. The expanded experiments support these retained core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning tolerance to inaccurate initialization, mask estimation, and limited training views. It replaces v1's foreground/background blending and mask-dependence limitations discussion with geometry/BRDF recovery, nonlinear-sRGB blur formation, and failures involving handheld objects or loose garments.

D1.justification: v2 adds camera trigger-delay details, identifies deformation networks as CNNs, and specifies iPhone/TRAM processing. It omits details including 6,890-Gaussian initialization, 50 synthetic frames per camera, the Camera 03 exclusion, and the 15 FPS capture rate. Code/data wording changes from publicly available to a future release.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including BARD-GS, AMASS, TRAM, and recent Gaussian/avatar research, while removing works including SelfRecon and the time-lapse examples. The central positioning against 2D deblurring and sharp-input avatar methods remains.

P1.justification: The title changes, much of the prose is condensed or rewritten, duplicated deblurring-related-work text is removed, and the standalone SMPL/3DGS preliminaries disappear. Experiments are reorganized around ablation, robustness, and further-discussion sections.

P2.justification: The pipeline diagram is redrawn, dataset-specific comparison and ablation tables are merged, and the combined hyperparameter table is split and expanded. New timing, initialization, mask, animation, and smartphone displays are added; the former limitations figure is removed. Existing qualitative comparisons are relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for central assumptions that v1 left insufficiently tested: tolerance to coarse SMPL initialization and imperfect masks, plus actual novel-pose animation. The smartphone demonstration extends practical validation, and rewritten limitations clarify important failure conditions. These gains outweigh the loss of some implementation details and the weaker resource-release statement, although the changed loss and preprocessing descriptions leave reproducibility questions.
